initial.prompt: Create a single transparent-background game equipment sprite of Tonbokiri, Honda Tadakatsu's Japanese straight spear. Entire weapon precisely vertical, sharp tip at top, butt at bottom, tall portrait composition. This is a proportional technical art brief: shaft length 180 cm, exposed steel blade length 43.7 cm, maximum blade width ONLY 3.7 cm. Total length 223.7 cm. Blade therefore occupies 19.5 percent of overall length and is extremely slender, blade aspect ratio nearly 12:1. Blade widest point is only 1.65 percent of total weapon height. It is a long narrow bamboo-leaf shaped blade, not a broad diamond, not an axe, not a sword broadhead. A delicate central ridge and fine carved groove with tiny traditional engraving. Shaft is slender straight dark lacquer wood around 2.7 cm diameter (1.2 percent total length), restrained bronze collars, tiny gold details at socket and butt, modest black grip wrapping around lower-middle. Upper shaft mostly plain dark lacquer. No wings, no large guard, no ribbons. Crisp high-resolution hand-painted Japanese arcade game weapon art, finely inked contours, controlled highlights and steel sheen, same mature detailed style as late 1990s Japanese beat-em-up character sprites rendered at modern high resolution. The long slender silhouette is the priority. Whole weapon with clear padding above tip and below butt; no cropping. Single isolated spear only, no text, no character, no shadows, no decorative background. True transparent RGBA. Generate a tall image.
